[[File:Dave Hakstol 2015.jpg|thumb|alt=Man in a suit standing in front of a black background|Dave Hakstol was the Kraken's inaugural head coach.]]

The [[Seattle Kraken]] are a professional [[ice hockey]] team based in [[Seattle]]. They are members of the [[Pacific Division (NHL)|Pacific Division]] of the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Kraken hockey team statistics and history |url=https://www.hockeydb.com/stte/seattle-kraken-12884.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240725182742/https://www.hockeydb.com/stte/seattle-kraken-12884.html |archive-date=2024-07-25 |access-date=2024-07-21 |website=[[HockeyDB]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rosen |first=Dan |date=2018-12-04 |title=Seattle NHL expansion approved by Board of Governors |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/seattle-nhl-expansion-approved-to-be-32nd-team-play-in-2021-22-302581450 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240923173845/https://www.nhl.com/news/seattle-nhl-expansion-approved-to-be-32nd-team-play-in-2021-22-302581450 |archive-date=2024-09-23 |access-date=2024-09-07 |website=[[National Hockey League]] |language=en}}</ref> The team was founded after the NHL approved a proposal by [[Seattle Kraken#Owners|Seattle Hockey Partners]] to grant an [[Expansion team|expansion franchise]] to the city of Seattle,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rosen |first=Dan |date=2018-12-04 |title=Seattle NHL expansion approved by Board of Governors |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/seattle-nhl-expansion-approved-to-be-32nd-team-play-in-2021-22-302581450 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240923173845/https://www.nhl.com/news/seattle-nhl-expansion-approved-to-be-32nd-team-play-in-2021-22-302581450 |archive-date=2024-09-23 |access-date=2024-06-06 |website=[[National Hockey League]] |language=en}}</ref> and began play during the league's [[2021–22 NHL season|2021–22 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Kraken Historical Statistics and All-Time Top Leaders |url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/teams/SEA/history.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241008213155/https://www.hockey-reference.com/teams/SEA/history.html |archive-date=2024-10-08 |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=[[Sports Reference|Hockey-Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

The team's first head coach, [[Dave Hakstol]], was hired on June 24, 2021.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Condor |first1=Bob |date=2021-07-24 |title=Getting it 'Right' |url=https://www.nhl.com/kraken/news/kraken-hire-dave-hakstol-as-first-head-coach-325455844 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220102165946/https://www.nhl.com/kraken/news/kraken-hire-dave-hakstol-as-first-head-coach/c-325455844 |archive-date=2022-01-02 |access-date=2022-10-20 |website=[[National Hockey League]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Kaplan |first1=Emily |date=2021-07-24 |title=Seattle Kraken name Dave Hakstol as their first head coach |url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/31701043/seattle-kracken-name-dave-hakstol-their-first-head-coach |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221020154041/https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/31701043/seattle-kracken-name-dave-hakstol-their-first-head-coach |archive-date=2022-10-20 |access-date=2022-10-20 |website=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> The Kraken's first season was very poor; the team finished eighth in their division due to only having 60 points, not enough to qualify for the playoffs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2021–22 Seattle Kraken Schedule |url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/teams/SEA/2022_games.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220603163238/https://www.hockey-reference.com/teams/SEA/2022_games.html |archive-date=2022-06-03 |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=[[Sports Reference|Hockey-Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> During the [[2022–23 NHL season|2022–23 season]], the Kraken achieved a record of 46–28–8 and 100 points, which was good for fourth place in the Pacific Division and the first playoff [[Wild card (sports)|wild card]] spot in the Western Conference.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022–23 Seattle Kraken Schedule |url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/teams/SEA/2023_games.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240908060920/https://www.hockey-reference.com/teams/SEA/2023_games.html |archive-date=2024-09-08 |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=[[Sports Reference|Hockey-Reference.com]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Didion |first=Alex |date=2023-04-18 |title=NHL Playoffs, explained: what to know about Kraken's first Stanley Cup pursuit |url=https://www.king5.com/article/sports/nhl/kraken/nhl-playoffs-explained-seattle-kraken/281-918753fa-1f30-4eda-928d-95b3a1c7fe8d |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230515030444/https://www.king5.com/article/sports/nhl/kraken/nhl-playoffs-explained-seattle-kraken/281-918753fa-1f30-4eda-928d-95b3a1c7fe8d |archive-date=2023-05-15 |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=[[KING-TV]] |language=en-US}}</ref> This turnaround from the previous season led Hakstol to be a finalist for the NHL's coaching prize, the [[Jack Adams Award]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyshynski |first=Greg |date=2023-05-05 |title=B's Montgomery leads coach of the year finalists |url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/37491874/jim-montgomery-dave-hakstol-lindy-ruff-finalists-jack-adams-award |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230517150947/https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/37491874/jim-montgomery-dave-hakstol-lindy-ruff-finalists-jack-adams-award |archive-date=2023-05-17 |access-date=2024-11-30 |website=[[ESPN]] |language=en}}</ref> During that season's [[2023 Stanley Cup playoffs|playoffs]], the Kraken faced off against the [[Colorado Avalanche]] in the first round. They upset the Avalanche in seven games, becoming the first team to win their inaugural playoff series against the [[List of Stanley Cup champions|defending Stanley Cup champion]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Slusher |first=Keenan |date=2023-05-01 |title=Kraken beat Avalanche 2–1, eliminate defending Stanley Cup champions |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nhl/news/kraken-beat-avalanche-2-1-eliminate-defending-stanley-cup-champions |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241126193542/https://www.nbcsports.com/nhl/news/kraken-beat-avalanche-2-1-eliminate-defending-stanley-cup-champions |archive-date=2024-11-26 |access-date=2024-03-23 |website=[[NBC Sports]]}}</ref> However, they lost to the [[Dallas Stars]] in the second round, ending their sophomore season.<ref>{{cite news |last=Myers |first=Tracey |date=2023-05-16 |title=Kraken eliminated from playoffs after playing from behind too often |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/why-seattle-is-eliminated-from-stanley-cup-playoffs-344421536 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230601013039/https://www.nhl.com/news/why-seattle-is-eliminated-from-stanley-cup-playoffs/c-344421536 |archive-date=2023-06-01 |access-date=2023-05-31 |work=[[National Hockey League]]}}</ref> At the NHL Awards ceremony on June 27, 2023, it was announced [[Jim Montgomery (ice hockey)|Jim Montgomery]], head coach of the [[Boston Bruins]], won the Jack Adams Trophy.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-27 |title=Jim Montgomery Wins 2023 Jack Adams Award |url=https://www.nhl.com/bruins/news/jim-montgomery-wins-2023-jack-adams-award-345026044 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240421142442/https://www.nhl.com/bruins/news/jim-montgomery-wins-2023-jack-adams-award-345026044 |archive-date=2024-04-21 |access-date=2024-11-30 |website=[[National Hockey League]] |language=en}}</ref>

The next season, the Kraken struggled offensively, ranking 29th in the league in goals, with only 217.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=2023–24 Seattle Kraken Roster, Stats, Injuries, Scores, Results, Shootouts |url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/teams/SEA/2024.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240927055324/https://www.hockey-reference.com/teams/SEA/2024.html |archive-date=2024-09-27 |access-date=2024-09-08 |website=[[Sports Reference|Hockey-Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Following the season, Hakstol was fired.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Ryan S. |date=2024-04-29 |title=Kraken fire coach Dave Hakstol after missing playoffs |url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/40051232/kraken-fire-coach-dave-hakstol-missing-playoffs |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240611134425/https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/40051232/kraken-fire-coach-dave-hakstol-missing-playoffs |archive-date=2024-06-11 |access-date=2024-07-11 |website=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> He was subsequently replaced by [[Dan Bylsma]], who had previously served as head coach of the Kraken's [[American Hockey League]] (AHL) affiliate, the [[Coachella Valley Firebirds]].<ref name="Bylsma528">{{cite web |date=2024-05-28 |title=Bylsma hired as coach of Kraken, replaces Hakstol |url=https://www.nhl.com/news/dan-bylsma-named-seattle-coach |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240528164826/https://www.nhl.com/news/dan-bylsma-named-seattle-coach |archive-date=2024-05-28 |access-date=2024-05-28 |website=[[National Hockey League]]}}</ref> However, after another difficult season that saw the Kraken finish sixth in the Pacific, Bylsma was fired one year into his tenure;<ref>{{cite web |date=April 21, 2025 |title=Seattle Kraken Announce Coaching Change |url=https://www.nhl.com/kraken/news/seattle-kraken-announce-coaching-change-pr |access-date=April 21, 2025 |website=[[National Hockey League]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Clark |first=Ryan S. |date=April 21, 2025 |title=Kraken fire coach Dan Bylsma after 1 season |url=https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/44787283/kraken-fire-coach-dan-bylsma-1-season-source-says |access-date=April 21, 2025 |website=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> he was subsequently replaced by [[Lane Lambert]] in May 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Condor |first=Bob |date=May 29, 2025 |title=Search is a Success: Lane Lambert New Coach |url=https://www.nhl.com/kraken/news/seattle-kraken-announce-lane-lambert-as-new-head-coach-bn |access-date=May 29, 2025 |website=[[National Hockey League]]}}</ref>
